The test image shows a soybean taproot/lower stem close-up with:
- Dark, rotted, dried taproot with a grayish-brown color
- **Blue-green spore masses visible on the root surface** — the most distinctive diagnostic feature
- Severely degraded root system

The SDS reference image (bottom-left panel) is a near-identical match — the same dark rotted taproot with blue-green fungal sporulation. The SDS knowledge base explicitly states: *"Blue-green spores of the fungus can occasionally be seen on the tap root after rain."* This is pathognomonic for *Fusarium virguliforme*, the causal agent of Sudden Death Syndrome.
